name: Joktan
title: Patriarch of Arab peoples
summary: Joktan was the son of Eber and brother to Peleg, and is regarded as the patriarch of thirteen Arab tribes. He belongs to the lineage of Shem, Noah's son, and his descendants settled in southern Arabia. While Peleg's line led onward to Abraham and the people of Israel, Joktan's line represents the Semitic peoples of the Arabian Peninsula.

keyEvents.title: Joktan's Place in Shem's Lineage
keyEvents.description: Joktan is mentioned as a son of Eber in the genealogy following Shem, Noah's son. This lineage shows how the nations spread after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Joktan's Thirteen Sons
keyEvents.description: The Bible lists Joktan's thirteen sons, who became ancestors for various ethnic groups in southern Arabia. These include well-known names such as Sheba, Ophir, and Havilah.

keyEvents.title: Settlement Area of the Descendants
keyEvents.description: Joktan's descendants settled in the mountainous region to the east, from Mesha to Sephar. This area likely corresponds to southern Arabia and Yemen.

keyEvents.title: Division of the Nations in the Days of Peleg
keyEvents.description: In Eber's days the earth was divided – this likely refers to the confusion of languages at Babel or a geographical division. Joktan and Peleg represent two branches of Eber's family that went in different directions.

keyEvents.title: Joktan in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Joktan's lineage is repeated in 1 Chronicles, confirming his significance in biblical history as the patriarch of many nations.

keyEvents.title: Joktan's place in Shem's extended lineage
keyEvents.description: In the detailed genealogy of Genesis 11, Eber is mentioned as the father of Peleg and Joktan, placing Joktan in the direct line from Shem to Abraham, even though Abraham's line goes through Peleg.
